blocks.text: Verify bounded bursts, recoverable actions, one cleanup, and one announcement per eligible ID.

blocks.title: Failure handling
rows: Expiry wins while the user clicks dismiss
Send both signals through remove(id); accept the first transition and ignore the later dismiss.
Store removal and timeout disposal each happen once.
A burst exceeds the visible limit
Render three records and append additional distinct records to the ordered queue.
The viewport stays bounded without losing an outcome.
Collapse only records that share a safe dedupe key.
Unrelated messages and recovery actions remain distinct.
Keep the persistent toast, expose retry, and retain failure context.
The user’s recovery path remains available.

blocks.text: Use a stable status live region with polite delivery for ordinary feedback and reserve alert for real interruption. Appearance never moves focus, but a hotkey such as F8 moves focus into the toast region, and closing a toast returns focus where it was. Review, Undo, retry, and close controls have descriptive labels, visible focus treatment, and normal keyboard order. Decorative motion respects reduced-motion preferences.

blocks.title: Tests that protect the design
items: Fire dismiss and expiry in both orders; assert one removal and one disposal.
Send four distinct commands; assert three visible and one queued record.
Rerender and reorder a record; assert its announcement ID is emitted once.
Fail an action; assert the persistent toast keeps keyboard-operable retry.
Use long localized text; assert wrapping does not cover controls.

blocks.text: Instrument queue depth, duplicate collapse, removal cause, action outcomes, and announcement emission. Use an inline or page error when recovery needs more context.

blocks.title: Expert stretch
blocks.text: Cover route scope, pause and resume, and measured policies for fair overflow. Define which records survive navigation. Pause the countdown while the toast has hover or focus or the tab is hidden, and resume from the stored remaining time. If telemetry shows starvation, compare admission using observed urgency, age, and recovery value instead of an invented priority rule.

blocks.alt: Timeline where the timeout starts removal first and a click on the exiting toast becomes a no-op.
blocks.caption: Dismiss-timeout race: either signal may arrive first, but removal and cleanup happen once.
blocks.fallbackText: Text fallback: The timeout runs first and starts removal; a click on the exiting toast sees the removing state and does nothing. If dismiss runs first, clearing the timeout means the callback never runs.
